source: Hy-Line W-80 India Commercial Layers Management Guide, Srinivasa Hy-Line, May 2024 (c) Hy-Line International; PDF W-80-Management-Guide_compressed.pdf, 'Rearing Period Nutritional Recommendations' (guide page 24) and 'Dietary Nutrient Concentrations for Production Period' (guide page 27).
aminoAcidBasis: Standardized Ileal Digestible. The guide prints SID and total side by side; niko's nutrient keys are digestible, so the SID column is the one loaded. The guide's own footnote says the total column applies only to a corn/soya diet and that SID must be followed where other materials are used, which is this mill.
notLoaded: Sodium and chloride (0.18-0.20% throughout rearing; 0.19-0.21% in lay) — niko has no nutrient key for either.
Linoleic acid and choline — no nutrient key.
Methionine+cystine is not a niko key; cystine is loaded as (Met+Cys) minus Met, which is what the sum means.
Crude fibre, fat and total phosphorus — the guide specifies none of them.
The guide's second starter diet ('Starter 2', to 410 g body weight) — the mill makes one chick feed, so the stricter Starter 1 spec is the one held.
caveats: Mixiblend P Layer Premix and Cantaxanthin have no analysis on file at all. The premix is under 1% of a batch by weight and can still change the answer out of all proportion to that: a layer premix may carry phytase, which frees the phytate phosphorus already present in the maize, DORB and soya. Until its datasheet is on file, a mix's available phosphorus cannot be compared to the guide's figure at all — it will read roughly half of what the birds actually get.

Crude protein is the guide's own estimate, not a requirement — its footnote says diets should be formulated to amino acid intake and that the crude protein shown will vary with the raw materials used. A mix below it is not necessarily short of anything.
Trace minerals and vitamins are specified on guide page 22 and have no nutrient key in niko, so a premix's main purpose is invisible here either way.

diets.note: Guide page 24. Hy-Line splits the starter in two — Starter 1 to 180 g body weight, Starter 2 to 410 g. The mill makes one chick feed covering both, so this holds the stricter of the pair; Starter 2 is ME 2850, CP 19.00, SID lysine 0.94 if a softer spec is ever wanted.
Guide page 24. Fed from 920 g body weight. Footnoted 'avoid excessive body weight gain after 12 weeks'.
Guide page 24. Fed from 1130 g body weight. The mill makes no developer feed today; the spec is held so a recipe can be judged if one is ever made.

Guide page 24. Not earlier than 15 weeks and not past the first egg — it has too little calcium to carry lay. It is where large-particle calcium is introduced: coarse limestone 2-4 mm, up to half the total limestone.

Guide page 27. First egg until peak, at the guide's typical intake of 95 g/bird/day. Concentrations rise if the flock eats less and fall if it eats more — the guide tabulates 85 to 105 g. Energy is printed as 260-270 kcal/bird/day, which at 95 g is 2,737-2,842 kcal/kg. Calcium and phosphorus are the guide's first-egg-to-32-weeks figures.

Guide page 27. Peak down to 90% lay, at the typical intake of 100 g/bird/day. Energy 270-280 kcal/bird/day is 2,700-2,800 kcal/kg at that intake. Calcium and phosphorus are the guide's weeks 33-55 figures.

Guide page 27. 89-85% lay, at the typical intake of 105 g/bird/day. Energy 270-280 kcal/bird/day is 2,571-2,667 kcal/kg at that intake. Calcium and phosphorus are the guide's weeks 56-85 figures. The mill makes no Layer 3 feed today.
